question: Does a source-bound failure-ledger and rival-prediction novelty workflow yield more distinct, executable and useful research hypotheses across case, simulator and scoring work than ordinary ideation at matched cost?
inclusions: Local and published closest-prior comparisons for each proposed research contribution
Controlled method contrasts, independent novelty/feasibility review and a balanced execution subset
Negative, duplicate, no-opening and inconclusive proposals
exclusions: Treating idea count or model self-rating as evidence of research value
Inferring case, score or hiring validity from a successful ideation workflow

selection_criteria: Pin date, query, exact source and closest comparator
Separate proposal judgment from executed value
source_policy.conflict_handling: Retain competing novelty and feasibility judgments with first-form evidence, then adjudicate without rewriting the original proposal.
source_policy.freshness_rule: Refresh literature and local source cuts before a new claimed addition or replication.

stop_conditions: Source facts or reference set cannot be frozen
Reviewers cannot distinguish candidate and prior mechanism
Execution selection is confounded by arm
limitations: No registered E12 run or independently reviewed proposal batch
External literature cut is targeted rather than exhaustive
claim_ceiling: Candidate inquiry only; no Lab admission, research-method finding or product authority.
